nodes.label: EnqueueUnitJobAsync race-free job pattern
nodes.rationale: Race-free ordering: subscribe, install JobRemoved watcher before the verb call, publish the returned job path into a lock-guarded pending cell, await with a 10-min timeout. D-Bus ordered delivery guarantees the signal arrives after the method return; the cell is needed because the return continuation and signal handler may run on different threads.

nodes.label: CS0101 double-compilation pitfall
nodes.rationale: Never set CompilerGeneratedFilesOutputPath to the project root (or any dir the SDK compiles): the emitted .cs gets compiled twice, producing a CS0101 redefinition storm. Emit under obj/ instead.

nodes.label: Unit-name to object-path encoding
nodes.rationale: Every non-alphanumeric character becomes '_' + two lowercase hex digits of the char code (e.g. . -> _2e, - -> _2d, @ -> _40). Prefer GetUnit/LoadUnit round-trips over computing paths by hand; compute only when a signal handler already carries the name.

nodes.label: Job-completion dance
nodes.rationale: StartUnit returns when the job is enqueued, not when it finishes. To know the outcome: Subscribe, install a JobRemoved handler BEFORE the method call, then match on the returned job path. Race-free because D-Bus delivers messages on one connection in order (method return always precedes the JobRemoved signal). Do not poll ListJobs or Unit.Job in a loop — the signal approach is exact and allocation-free.

nodes.label: Manager.Subscribe() signal gating
nodes.rationale: systemd suppresses most signals (JobRemoved, unit PropertiesChanged) unless at least one client has called Manager.Subscribe() on its connection; it is a per-connection flag and emission stops when the last subscriber disconnects or unsubscribes. A client that only calls ListUnits never needs it; any signal watcher must Subscribe() first or silently receive nothing.
